question: What is the primary purpose of a general physical examination?

options.A: To diagnose complex psychiatric disorders independently
options.B: To replace the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: To gather baseline data about a patient's health status

explanation: A general exam is primarily done to establish a baseline of physical health so nurses can track changes over time. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why does a nurse perform a head-to-toe examination instead of only checking the patient's main complaint?

options.A: To detect subtle changes and physical signs of illness across all body systems
options.B: To fulfill hospital administrative requirements without clinical benefit
options.C: To quickly discharge the patient from the ward without delay
options.D: To avoid having to ask the patient about their medical history

explanation: Looking at the whole person helps uncover hidden issues that might be related to, or worsened by, the main complaint. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why should a patient empty their bladder before a physical examination?

options.A: To collect a routine midstream urine sample automatically
options.B: To prevent the patient from falling asleep during the assessment
options.C: To reduce the overall weight of the patient before weighing
options.D: To ensure patient comfort during abdominal palpation

explanation: An empty bladder prevents discomfort and pressure when the nurse presses on the lower abdomen. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the main reason for explaining each step of the exam to the patient?

options.A: To fulfill a legal requirement for surgical consent
options.B: To reduce anxiety and build trust between nurse and patient
options.C: To train the patient to perform their own physical assessment
options.D: To speed up the total time spent at the bedside

explanation: Clear communication helps the patient relax, making the assessment easier and more accurate. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h2)

question: When should hand hygiene be performed during a physical examination?

options.A: At the end of the entire shift
options.B: Only when the patient has a known infection
options.C: Before and after touching the patient
options.D: Only if the nurse's hands look visibly dirty

explanation: Hand hygiene is the single most effective way to stop the spread of germs between patients and healthcare workers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: Why must reusable equipment like stethoscopes be wiped with disinfectant between patients?

options.A: To prevent cross-contamination and hospital-acquired infections
options.B: To keep the metal parts from rusting in humid weather
options.C: To remove any manufacturer dust from the surface
options.D: To ensure the sound quality remains clear for hearing

explanation: Medical tools can easily carry germs from one patient to another if they are not cleaned properly. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: When does the general survey of a patient actually begin?

options.A: After listening to the patient's heart and lungs
options.B: When the blood pressure cuff is inflated
options.C: When writing the final discharge notes
options.D: The moment the nurse first sees the patient

explanation: The general survey starts immediately through observation before any hands-on examination takes place. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: A nurse walks into a room and notices a patient clutching their chest and breathing heavily. What category of the general survey does this fall under?
explanation: Clutching the chest and heavy breathing are immediate physical indicators of acute distress. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which measurement is frequently referred to as the fifth vital sign?
explanation: Pain is routinely assessed alongside traditional vital signs to monitor patient comfort and well-being. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why is it important to use the correct blood pressure cuff size?

options.A: It prevents the patient from feeling any pressure at all
options.B: An incorrect size leads to inaccurate blood pressure readings
options.C: Hospital regulations require matching cuffs to patient age only
options.D: Small cuffs are easier to wrap around the arm quickly

explanation: A cuff that is too small gives a falsely high reading, while one that is too large gives a falsely low reading. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: What is the correct order of assessment techniques for most body parts?
explanation: For most body systems, you look first, feel second, tap third, and listen last. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: Why is the sequence of techniques changed when examining the abdomen?

options.A: Auscultation is done first so pressing on the belly does not change bowel sounds
options.B: Percussion is omitted entirely to prevent patient discomfort
options.C: Inspection is skipped because visual data is unreliable
options.D: Palpation must be done first to locate hidden organs before listening

explanation: Touching or pressing the abdomen can stimulate bowel activity, giving a false impression of bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: What type of language should a nurse use when documenting physical exam findings?

options.B: Subjective opinions about the patient's attitude
options.D: Complex poetic metaphors to describe wounds

explanation: Objective descriptions prevent confusion and provide clear facts for other healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why is timely documentation of assessment findings important for patient care?

options.A: It is only required for billing and insurance purposes
options.B: It prevents patients from reading their own medical charts
options.C: It ensures continuity of care and accurate communication across shifts
options.D: It allows the nurse to leave the hospital premises much earlier

explanation: Prompt charting lets the next nurse or doctor know the exact status of the patient without relying on memory. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)
